company.name: Eternal
company.summary: The listed parent connecting Zomato, Blinkit, District and Hyperpure.
company.description: Eternal is the company formerly named Zomato Limited. Its businesses cover restaurant food delivery, quick commerce, going-out experiences and supplies for restaurants. These businesses share a digital-commerce theme but have different operating costs and revenue models.
company.ownership: Buying Eternal shares is exposure to the listed group, not a separately listed Zomato or Blinkit share. Zomato remains a consumer brand after the corporate name changed. District and Hyperpure are also part of the group portfolio.
products: Quick commerce · groceries and everyday goods
company.money: The group earns through combinations of commissions, service and delivery charges, advertising, and product sales, depending on the business. The value of orders placed on an app is not the same as the company’s recognised revenue or profit.
watch: How do food delivery and quick commerce contribute after fulfilment and marketing costs?
Are customers ordering more frequently without relying only on discounts?
How much cash is needed to build and operate the growing network?
risks: Discounts, advertising and delivery incentives can reduce profitability.
Store density, inventory, delivery and staffing influence quick-commerce economics.
Food safety, gig-work rules and relationships with merchants affect operations.
company.question: Is the full value of a restaurant order automatically Eternal’s revenue?
company.answer: No. Marketplace order value includes amounts belonging to restaurants and other participants. Accounting treatment differs between marketplace services and product-sales businesses.
update: One listed company, several different business models
Use business-level disclosures to separate Zomato, Blinkit, District and Hyperpure rather than treating every order as identical.
